  <h3>BigBang: Pursuing Open-Ended Intelligence through Self-Evolving Synthesis of Verifiable Frontier Tasks</h3>
  <p>BigBang is a general-purpose 35B-A3B model post-trained on verifiable frontier tasks generated by an adversarial, self-evolving generator-critic framework. Calibrated with held-out research tasks, the pipeline iteratively improves task difficulty and evaluation quality, yielding broad gains in scientific research, reasoning, coding, and tool use.</p>

  <h3>DataPrep-Bench: Benchmarking LLMs as Training Data Preparators</h3>
  <p>DataPrep-Bench is the first unified, downstream-grounded benchmark for evaluating how LLMs, agents, and data-centric workflows construct supervised training data and predict candidate datasets&#x27; downstream utility. It also introduces a skill-guided construction agent and the Distributional Alignment Score, which outperforms existing quality, diversity, and heuristic evaluators across most tested domains.</p>

<article class="paper-card" id="powlu-an-activation-function-for-stable-pre-training-of-llms">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>PowLU: An Activation Function for Stable Pre-Training of LLMs</h3>
  <p>This paper identifies SwiGLU&#x27;s near-quadratic amplification on large positive inputs as a source of outliers and numerical instability in low-precision large-scale LLM pre-training. It proposes Power Linear Unit (PowLU), a rational-power activation that preserves adaptive nonlinearity while stabilizing spike regions, with scaling-law and Ling-model experiments showing competitive performance and improved training scalability.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25704" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="pre-training-llm-without-learning-rate-decay-enhances-supervised-fine-tuning">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.03</span>
    <span>Optimization</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Pre-training LLM without Learning Rate Decay Enhances Supervised Fine-Tuning</h3>
  <p>This paper shows that Warmup-Stable-Only pre-training, which keeps the learning rate constant after warmup, consistently improves downstream SFT performance over decay-based schedules across 1B and 8B models. Its loss-landscape analysis attributes the gain to flatter minima that preserve model adaptability.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16127" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
  </div>
</article>

<article class="paper-card" id="escaping-the-kl-agreement-trap-in-on-policy-distillation">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.06</span>
    <span>Distillation</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Escaping the KL Agreement Trap in On-Policy Distillation</h3>
  <p>This paper identifies a low-KL agreement trap in on-policy distillation, where a teacher locally agrees with a student&#x27;s corrupted rollout and provides little corrective supervision. It proposes KAT, an adaptive online termination rule that filters these uninformative suffixes, improving mathematical reasoning accuracy while reducing average rollout length by 59.73%.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09471" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="on-policy-distillation-with-best-of-n-teacher-rollout-selection">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>Distillation</span>
  </div>
  <h3>On-Policy Distillation with Best-of-N Teacher Rollout Selection</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes BRTS, which samples multiple teacher trajectories and selects supervision by prioritizing correctness and then alignment with the student&#x27;s current behavior. An auxiliary teacher-context branch and ground-truth-conditioned recovery improve OPD on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09725" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>

</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="trust-region-on-policy-distillation">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.05</span>
    <span>Distillation</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Trust Region On-Policy Distillation</h3>
  <p>This paper proposes TrOPD to stabilize on-policy distillation under large teacher-student distribution mismatch by restricting reverse-KL supervision to reliable regions. It handles outliers through clipping, masking, or forward-KL estimation and uses teacher-prefix off-policy guidance to steer exploration back toward trustworthy regions.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01249" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="revisiting-on-policy-distillation-empirical-failure-modes-and-simple-fixes">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2026.03</span>
    <span>Distillation</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Revisiting On-Policy Distillation: Empirical Failure Modes and Simple Fixes</h3>
  <p>This paper identifies three failure modes in sampled-token OPD: imbalanced token supervision, unreliable teacher guidance on student-generated prefixes, and tokenizer or special-token mismatch. It combines teacher top-K local support matching with top-p rollout sampling and special-token masking, improving stability and outperforming standard OPD by 19.8%.</p>
  <div class="paper-links">
<a class="resource-link" href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25562" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/arxiv.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Paper</a>
<a class="resource-link" href="https://github.com/hhh675597/revisiting_opd" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img src="../../assets/icons/github.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true" />Code</a>
  </div>
</article>
<article class="paper-card" id="knowledge-distillation-of-large-language-models">
  <div class="paper-meta">
    <span>2023.06</span>
    <span>Distillation</span>
  </div>
  <h3>Knowledge Distillation of Large Language Models</h3>
  <p>This paper studies white-box knowledge distillation for generative LLMs and proposes MiniLLM, replacing the standard forward KLD objective with reverse KLD to avoid overestimating low-probability teacher regions. The method derives an effective optimization procedure and improves instruction-following quality, calibration, exposure bias, and long-text generation across model families from 120M to 13B parameters.</p>
